Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Pravin Kumar Mishra
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Anish Kumar Gupta,J.
1.
Heard Sri Pravin Kumar Mishra, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Kripa Shankar, learned A.G.A. for the State.

2. The instant application under Section 438 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicant seeking anticipatory bail in Case Crime No. 140 of 2023 under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506, 352, 354A I.P.C. and 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station-Bhavanpur, District-Meerut.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the instant FIR has been lodged by the wife of the applicant herein due to matrimonial dispute on false and fabricated facts and the charge sheet has already been filed in the matter.

However, during the investigation various independent witnesses have also been examined who have categorically stated that the victim was having some extra marital affair which was objected by the applicant herein, thereupon the present FIR has been Lavkush Chauhan vs State Of U.P. And Another on 4 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146037259/
1 lodged on false and fabricated facts relating to matrimonial dispute.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, he seeks grant of anticipatory bail in the matter.

4. Per contra learned A.G.A. opposing the application for anticipatory bail submits that FIR has been lodged due to matrimonial dispute between the applicant and his wife and after thorough investigation charge sheet has also been filed against the applicant and therefore, no case for grant of anticipatory bail is made out.
5. Considered the rival submissions of learned counsel for the parties.

From perusal of the record, it is apparent that during investigation statement of some witnesses have been recorded wherein they have stated that the wife of the applicant was having extra marital affair and the FIR has been falsely lodged against the applicant on the basis of matrimonial dispute.

6. Looking to the facts and evidence of the case, reasonable apprehension of arrest, taking into consideration the gravity and nature of accusation, there being no criminal antecedents of the applicant and there being no possibility of his fleeing from justice, the applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail in this case.

7. In the event of arrest of the applicant -Lavkush Chauhan involved in the aforesaid case shall be released on anticipatory bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned Court below with the following conditions :-
(i) That the applicant shall cooperate in the expeditious disposal of the trial and shall regularly attend the court on each dates unless inevitable.

(ii) That the applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) That the applicant shall not involve in any criminal activity.
(iv) In case of breach of any of the conditions mentioned above, the concerned Court below will be at liberty to cancel the anticipatory bail of the applicant after recording reasons.
(v) The applicant shall not leave India without previous permission of the Court.

(v) In case, it is found that applicant has obtained this order concealing any material facts, the investigating officer shall be at liberty to file an appropriate application for cancellation of anticipatory bail granted to the applicant.

8. It is clarified that observations made in this order at this stage is limited to the purpose of determination of this anticipatory bail application only and will in no way be construed as an expression on the merits of the case.

The concerned Court below shall be absolutely free to arrive at Lavkush Chauhan vs State Of U.P. And Another on 4 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146037259/
